subject: Career
title: The Network Audit
description: A 60-second lesson on The Network Audit.

hook.text: When was the last time you looked at your network and asked: 'Is this helping me grow?'

buildup.text: A network audit maps your connections by type: mentors, peers, sponsors, industry contacts, cross-industry.

discovery.text: Most people find gaps: too many peers, not enough senior contacts or cross-industry connections.

twist.text: A balanced network needs diversity: different levels, industries, geographies, and perspectives.

climax.text: Audit quarterly. Identify gaps. Set a goal: 'This quarter I'll connect with three people in X.'

punchline.text: You can't improve a network you haven't mapped.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a network audit?
options: To identify gaps and ensure diversity in your connections
To remove people from your network

details.summary: A network audit systematically maps your professional relationships by strength, diversity, and strategic value, revealing gaps and over-concentrations. Most professionals discover their networks are smaller and less diverse than assumed.
details.whyItMatters: You cannot improve what you do not measure. A network audit converts vague networking intuition into a concrete action plan for building the connections you actually need.
takeaways: Categorize contacts by relationship strength and strategic relevance
Identify clusters where you have too many similar connections
Plan targeted outreach to fill gaps revealed by the audit

faq.question: How often should you conduct a professional network audit?
faq.answer: Annually is sufficient for most professionals. Conduct an additional audit before major career transitions such as job changes, industry pivots, or entrepreneurial ventures. The insights compound when you track changes over multiple years.

faq.question: What is the simplest way to perform a network audit?
faq.answer: Create a spreadsheet with columns for name, relationship strength, industry, function, and last interaction date. Export your LinkedIn connections as a starting point. Sort by last interaction to identify dormant ties and by industry to spot homophily.
